chunks: He said: Abu Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abu Sheik reported to me with permission from Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Hakimi, who reported from Abdul Rahman ibn Abdillah Abu Saeed al-Basri, who reported from Wahb ibn Jarir, from his father, who reported from Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar al-Madani, who reported from Saeed ibn Mina, from more than one of his companions:

A group of Quraysh confronted the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his progeny, among them Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, and al-Aas ibn Sa'id. They said: "O Muhammad, come, let us worship what you worship, and you worship what we worship, and we will share together in this matter. If the truth is with us, then you will have taken your share from it; and if the truth is with you, then we will have taken our share from it." So Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed:
"Say: O disbelievers! I do not worship what you worship; nor do you worship what I worship" to the end of the surah.

Then Ubay ibn Khalaf came to him with a withered bone and crumbled it with his hand, then blew it and said: "O Muhammad, do you claim that your Lord will give life to this after what you see?" So Allah, the Exalted, revealed:

"And he produced an equal for Us and forgot his creation; he said: Who gives life to the bones when they are decayed? Say: He who originated them the first time will give them life, and He has knowledge of every creation" to the end of the surah.

أَنْشَأَهَا.context: The divine argument that the Creator who originated life the first time can surely revive it

اعْتَرَضُوا.context: The Quraysh physically intercepted the Prophet to deliver their proposal for religious compromise

الْكَافِرُونَ.context: The opening address of Surah 109, categorically distinguishing the Prophet's monotheism from polytheism

رَمِيمٍ.context: Describes the bone that Ubay ibn Khalaf brought to mock the concept of resurrection

نَشْتَرِكُ.context: The Quraysh proposal to mutually participate in each other's worship as a compromise

ai.seo_question: What were the circumstances of the revelation of Surah al-Kafirun and the Quranic response to those who denied resurrection?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates two pivotal encounters between the Prophet Muhammad and the Meccan polytheists. In the first, a delegation of Quraysh leaders including Utbah ibn Rabi'ah, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, and al-Aas ibn Sa'id proposed a religious compromise: mutual worship-sharing. Allah responded by revealing Surah al-Kafirun (109), firmly rejecting any syncretism. In the second incident, Ubay ibn Khalaf brought a decayed bone, crumbled and blew it, mockingly challenging the concept of resurrection. Allah answered with verses from Surah Yasin (36:78-79), declaring that the One who created bones the first time has full power and knowledge to revive them.
